description: Single source of truth for the Orbita CRM agent fields. The prompt's field dictionary, the output schema, the validator, the scorer, the review table, the permissions page, the record drawers and the CSV export are all derived from this file. Values are always stored as strings (or null); the type below says how a string is checked and normalised.
seller_only_note: Deal amount, close date, probability, discount, price, contract term, owner and contacts are set by the seller only. The agent never proposes them; when the conversation asks for them, they go to ignored_out_of_scope.

levels.label: Always allow
levels.help: Written as soon as the update is prepared. You can undo it.

levels.label: Needs approval
levels.help: Proposed for your review; written only after you approve.

levels.label: Never
levels.help: The agent leaves this field alone.

fixed_rules: A proposal that contradicts a value you approved always waits for your decision.
The stage moves one step forward at most, and never to Closed Won or Closed Lost.
Amount, close date, probability, discount, owner and contacts are never written by the agent.

fields.label: Summary
fields.definition: What the conversation was about, the key facts and the outcome.
fields.evidence: Only facts stated in the transcript. No opinions or predictions.
fields.good: Intro call with the Commercial Director. Group and corporate requests arrive by email and live in spreadsheets, so requests get lost. He wants one place for every request and account, for 15 users, without a heavy implementation. A working session was agreed for 15 Oct.
fields.bad: Great call, the customer loved us and will probably buy. (opinion, not facts)

fields.label: Objections
fields.definition: Concerns, risks or blockers the customer raised in this conversation.
fields.evidence: A customer statement. Never the seller's speculation.
fields.format: 40 words max; several objections separated by '; '.
fields.good: Small, busy team; cannot take on a heavy implementation
fields.bad: Price may be an issue (when price was never mentioned)

fields.label: Commitments
fields.definition: Explicit promises made by either side in this conversation.
fields.evidence: An explicit 'I will' or 'we will'. Intentions such as 'maybe', 'we'll see' or conditional promises do not count.
fields.format: Party (person): action (by date); several commitments separated by '; '.
fields.good: Orbita (Ana): send the working-session agenda by 9 Oct
fields.bad: Customer will think about it

fields.label: Next step
fields.definition: The agreed next action or meeting that moves the opportunity forward.
fields.evidence: Agreed by both sides: proposed by one side and accepted by the other. A step the customer declined is not a next step.
fields.good: Working session with the Mar Azul sales coordinators on 15 Oct at 10:00
fields.bad: Second meeting with the team (when the customer said 'not yet')

fields.label: Follow-up owner
fields.definition: The Orbita person responsible for the next follow-up.
fields.evidence: That person says they will do it, or is explicitly assigned. Must be in the team roster; customer-side people are not allowed.
fields.format: Full name exactly as in the roster.
fields.good: Ana Ribeiro
fields.bad: Gustavo Teixeira (customer side) or 'Ana' (not the full roster name)

fields.label: Follow-up due date
fields.definition: The date by which the follow-up owner must act.
fields.evidence: An explicit date or day ('by Friday'), resolved from the conversation date. 'No rush', 'soon' or no timeframe means no evidence.
fields.good: Meeting on Tue 2026-10-06, 'by Friday' -> 2026-10-09
fields.bad: Inventing a date when the customer said 'no rush'

fields.label: Metrics
fields.ask: What number should the CRM move, and by how much?
fields.definition: The measurable result the customer expects from the CRM: the number they want to move, and by how much.
fields.evidence: A target or measure stated by the customer (a rate, a time, a count, money saved). A vague wish ('be more efficient') is not a metric.
fields.format: 40 words max; several metrics separated by '; '.
fields.good: Answer every group request within 24 hours; cut lost group bookings by half
fields.bad: Improve sales (no measure)

fields.label: Economic buyer
fields.ask: Who gives the final yes and owns the budget? Have we met them?
fields.definition: The customer-side person who gives the final yes and owns the budget for this purchase.
fields.evidence: That person says they decide or hold the budget, or another customer names them as the one who decides or signs. The speaker must be identified: a statement from an unattributed speaker does not establish who decides.
fields.good: Gustavo Teixeira (Commercial Director)
fields.bad: Ana Ribeiro (seller side) or 'the boss' (not a named person)

fields.label: Decision criteria
fields.ask: What will you judge the vendors on? What is a must-have?
fields.definition: What the customer will judge the vendors on: must-have capabilities and business or technical requirements.
fields.evidence: Stated by the customer as a requirement or a deciding factor ('must', 'has to', 'a must', 'deal-breaker', 'we will choose on').
fields.format: 40 words max; several criteria separated by '; '.
fields.good: Shared view of group requests and accounts; follow-up reminders; light implementation
fields.bad: A good product (not a criterion)

fields.label: Decision process
fields.ask: What are the steps between today and the decision, and who is involved?
fields.definition: The steps and people that lead to the decision, in order: evaluations, validations and approvals.
fields.evidence: Stated by the customer.
fields.good: The sales coordinators test it in a working session; then the Commercial Director decides
fields.bad: Standard process

fields.label: Paper process
fields.ask: Once you decide, what do procurement and legal need before the signature?
fields.definition: How the purchase gets signed once it is decided: procurement, legal, security or data reviews, contract and signature, and what could delay them.
fields.evidence: Stated by the customer.
fields.good: Procurement asks for two quotes; Legal reviews the contract in two weeks; the Commercial Director signs
fields.bad: Paperwork (no steps)

fields.label: Pain
fields.ask: What goes wrong today, and what does it cost you?
fields.definition: The business problem that makes the customer act, in their terms: what goes wrong today and what it costs them.
fields.evidence: Stated by the customer, or the seller's restatement confirmed by the customer.
fields.good: Group and corporate requests live in email and spreadsheets and get lost; the team needs one place for every request and account, with follow-up reminders
fields.bad: Interested in our product (not a pain)

fields.label: Champion
fields.ask: Who inside the company is pushing for this, and will they help us reach the economic buyer?
fields.definition: The customer-side person who actively sells Orbita inside the company and has influence on the decision.
fields.evidence: The person says they are pushing for the project or will win others over, or another customer names them as the sponsor. Enthusiasm alone ('I love it') is not enough. The speaker must be identified.
fields.good: Renata Lima (Sales Coordinator)
fields.bad: Ana Ribeiro (seller side) or 'someone in sales'

fields.label: Competition
fields.ask: Who else are you looking at, including keeping today's tools?
fields.definition: The alternatives the customer is considering for this purchase: other vendors, building in-house, or staying with what they have.
fields.evidence: Named by the customer.
fields.good: Northwind CRM; PipeSpark
fields.bad: Several vendors (not named)

fields.label: Seats (users)
fields.definition: How many people will use the CRM (licences).
fields.evidence: A number of users stated in the conversation. A range without a number the customer commits to is not evidence.
fields.bad: 600 (that is the company headcount, see employee_count)

fields.label: Departments
fields.definition: The teams that will use the CRM.
fields.evidence: Named in the conversation. A team clearly described counts ('my sales coordinators' -> Sales).
fields.format: One or more of: Sales; Customer Success; Customer Service; Marketing; Finance; Operations; Leadership; IT. Separated by '; ', in this order.
fields.good: Sales; Marketing
fields.bad: Front desk (not in the list)

fields.label: Integrations
fields.definition: Systems the CRM must connect to.
fields.evidence: Named by the customer.
fields.good: In-house booking system; email and calendar
fields.bad: Their systems

fields.label: Budget
fields.definition: The money the customer says is available for this CRM.
fields.evidence: Stated by the customer. A deal amount the seller is asked to record is an instruction about a seller-only field, not a budget.
fields.format: 'USD <amount or range> per <period>', for example 'USD 80,000-100,000 per year'; or 'No budget allocated' when the customer says so.
fields.good: USD 50,000 per year
fields.bad: USD 200,000 per year (taken from 'put us down for a two hundred thousand deal')

fields.label: Go-live target
fields.definition: When the customer needs the CRM live.
fields.evidence: A month or date the customer states as their target or deadline. 'Sometime next year' is not evidence.
fields.format: YYYY-MM (the month of the target or deadline).
fields.good: 'We need it live by March 2027' -> 2027-03
fields.bad: 2027-06 from 'sometime next year'

fields.label: Employees
fields.definition: Total number of employees at the client company.
fields.evidence: Stated in the conversation.
fields.bad: 15 (that is the number of CRM users, see seats)

fields.label: Current solution
fields.definition: What the client uses today to manage customers and deals.
fields.evidence: Stated in the conversation.
fields.good: Email and spreadsheets
fields.bad: Old system

fields.label: Stage
fields.definition: Sales stage of the opportunity.
fields.evidence: See the stage rules. Propose a new stage only when every exit criterion of the current stage is evidenced in this conversation.
fields.format: One value of the stage list.
fields.good: Qualified Opportunity (from New Lead, with a quote for each criterion)
fields.bad: Contract (from Proposal: more than one step)
